function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker service itself. To start Docker Desktop or Docker Engine on Windows, you typically use services or Docker Desktop UI. On Windows, you can start the Docker service via PowerShell: Start-Service Docker. Or if using Docker Desktop, you might need to launch Docker Desktop app. The user likely wants to start Docker engine. So we should explain that docker start starts containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, use Start-Service Docker or restart Docker Desktop. Provide commands.

We have a tool to execute commands. We can call cmd_controller_execute with command "Start-Service Docker" or "net start com.docker.service". But we need to be careful: The tool expects a Windows command line instruction. For starting the Docker service, we can use "net start com.docker.service". That will start the Docker service. Alternatively, "Start-Service Docker" is PowerShell. The tool uses os.system, so it runs in cmd.exe context. So "net start com.docker.service" is appropriate.

Thus we can call the function with command "net start com.docker.service". Also mention that docker start is for containers. Provide explanation.
